entries.clue: Performance of an arse loosely enthralling one (7)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: to enthral is to hold captive, so RECTAL holds I inside it

blocks.note: rectal = of the rectum, which is 'an arse' if you speak loosely

annotation.surface: A review of some show that consisted of a backside being waggled about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loosely' is not an anagram signal here: it apologises for glossing 'rectal' as 'of an arse'. RECT(I)AL is the whole trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance, typically of music or poetry.

entries.clue: see 18ac. (8)
(& 24dn.) Fail to separate oddballs, as Republicans do around Trump (5)

indicatorNotes.to separate: LOSE goes between the letters of CRANKS, parting C from RANKS

annotation.surface: A jibe that Republicans cannot bring themselves to split from the eccentrics around Trump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fail to separate' reads as one phrase meaning 'stay together', uncomfortably close to the answer's own sense, but the break falls after 'Fail'. The definition is a description, not a dictionary synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: To close ranks is to unite in mutual defence, which is what a party does around a leader under attack.

entries.clue: Mean Bottom or Scrooge? (9)

annotation.surface: A question of whether some miser is Bottom, the weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream, or Scrooge.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital B makes 'Bottom' look like Shakespeare's character, but it is just a backside. 'Tightarse' is British slang for a skinflint.
annotation.definitionFit: Scrooge, Dickens's miser, is the archetypal tightarse.

entries.clue: Lords chief dodgy 'cure' for dishonest gain (5)

indicatorNotes.chief: the chief letter of a word is its first
indicatorNotes.dodgy: dodgy = unsound, so the letters of CURE are rearranged

annotation.surface: A remedy peddled by the head of the House of Lords as a way to make money on the side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lords chief' looks like a peer in charge, but it only supplies the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucre, as in 'filthy lucre', is money, especially when gained dishonestly.

entries.clue: Bribe returned – Davey was affected? (5)

indicatorNotes.returned: turned back, so SOP is read in the other direction

blocks.note: a sop = something given to buy someone off
Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats

annotation.surface: A bribe handed back, and a question about whether the Lib Dem leader was influenced by it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Affected' suggests 'influenced' by the bribe; here it means putting on airs. Ed Davey is a British party leader, the Liberal Democrats' head.
annotation.definitionFit: To pose is to behave affectedly, so 'posed' = 'was affected'.

entries.clue: The game of Roger Roger (5)

blocks.note: to roger and to poke are both slang for having sex
'Roger' is the old radio code word for R

annotation.surface: A teasing reference to what Roger Roger likes to play, as though that were his name.
annotation.walkthrough: The doubled name looks like a comic person; the first Roger is the slang verb, the second the radio word for R.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: poker is one card game among many, and 'The game' reads as the one Roger plays.

entries.clue: Government aimed to ditch a communiqué (9)

indicatorNotes.to ditch: to ditch is to get rid of, so the A is removed from MEANT

blocks.note: the A that MEANT loses, leaving MENT

annotation.surface: Officials planned to scrap an official announcement.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a government withdrawing a press release; the 'a' is literally the letter taken away.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a communiqué, French for 'something communicated', is the formal word for what a government issues to the press.

entries.clue: Part inside testicles – can't stand (6)

indicatorNotes.Part: the answer is part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A complaint that some part of the anatomy down there is unbearable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like the signal to look within, but it is the fodder: the answer straddles 'inside' and 'testicles'.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'can't stand' is everyday speech for loathing, the same strong dislike the verb names.

entries.clue: In canteen, handy for the boozer (8)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective phrase standing for a noun: something handy for the boozer

blocks.note: a canteen is also a water bottle carried by soldiers or campers

annotation.surface: A tip that the works canteen is conveniently close to the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canteen' suggests a dining hall and 'boozer' a pub, but a canteen is also a drinking bottle and the boozer is a drinker. 'In' is the adjective 'fashionable', not a preposition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a small spirits flask kept in a hip pocket is always to hand for a drinker.

entries.clue: Cream on goolies – inside, not on the outside (5)

indicatorNotes.inside: the answer sits inside the words before it, spanning three of them

annotation.surface: Instructions for applying ointment to the testicles: rub it in, don't leave it on top.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as application advice; 'goolies' is British slang for testicles.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: to be among a crowd is to be in its midst, not on its outside edge.

entries.clue: Cats start to tongue Harry which encourages mouse activity (9)

indicatorNotes.start: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to harry = to bait, to torment

annotation.surface: Cats teasing and licking at something that gets the mice moving.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all cat and mouse; 'mouse activity' is really clicking a computer mouse. 'Harry' is the verb, not a name.
annotation.definitionFit: Clickbait is online content designed to make readers click on a link.

entries.clue: His Majesty's now possibly pissed at three (7)

indicatorNotes.pissed: British slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: The King may be drunk by three in the afternoon.
annotation.walkthrough: His Majesty's is a London West End theatre, renamed from Her Majesty's after the Queen died; 'now' points to the new name and 'possibly' marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: His Majesty's in the Haymarket is one London playhouse, and 'possibly' flags it as just one instance.

entries.clue: Labour might require such a device as sticking Penny in the military! (7)

annotation.definition: Labour might require such a device

indicatorNotes.sticking: sticking one thing in another means pushing it inside, as a pin is stuck in a cushion
indicatorNotes.in: 'in the military' says where Penny goes: within the word for the armed forces

annotation.surface: A political quip that the Labour Party needs a device like putting Penny into the armed forces.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital L makes 'Labour' the party; it is childbirth. Penny Mordaunt, a Navy reservist and Conservative minister, is the likely surface target.
annotation.definitionFit: Forceps are the tongs used to help deliver a baby during labour.

entries.clue: Dicky, on going arse over tip, gets tender (5)

indicatorNotes.going arse over tip: tumbling head over heels, so RE is turned upside down

annotation.surface: Someone called Dicky takes a tumble and ends up sore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name and 'tender' like a bruise; 'arse over tip' is British for head over heels.
annotation.definitionFit: To tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid or resignation.

entries.clue: A senior, given time, gets caught in fact, in 'flagrante' –"marvellous!" (9)

indicatorNotes.caught in: to be caught in something is to be trapped within it, so AST is held inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.'flagrante': flagrante is Latin for blazing, so the letters of IN FACT are set wildly ablaze into a new order

blocks.note: IN FACT rearranged, then split FANT…IC

annotation.surface: An elderly person with time on their hands is caught in the act and cries out in delight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In flagrante' (Latin, 'caught in the act') is broken up: the 'in' belongs with 'fact' as letters to rearrange, and 'flagrante' alone is the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Fantastic! is an exclamation of delight, like marvellous!

entries.clue: House cover-up is effected by one old PM (8)

annotation.definition2: House cover-up is effected by one

blocks.clueFragment: House cover-up is effected by one
blocks.note: the cover-up is a straw or reed roof, and 'one' is the craftsman who lays it
a former British Prime Minister, here the Conservative leader of 1979-90

annotation.surface: A former prime minister is behind a scandal about the House.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House cover-up' sounds like a parliamentary scandal; it is a roof, and the one who puts it on is a thatcher.
annotation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was Prime Minister of the UK.

entries.clue: Arse wobbled in true style, darling (8)

indicatorNotes.wobbled in: wobbled = shaken about, and ARSE is jumbled in with TRUE

annotation.surface: An appreciative remark to someone whose bottom wobbles in a truly stylish way.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a leering compliment; all eight letters of ARSE and TRUE are shaken together.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Treasure' is an endearment, like darling.

entries.clue: Like a strict TT, stony, son-of-a-bitch, eastern Republican (4,5)

annotation.surface: A string of insults for a hard-hearted, puritanical Republican from the East.
annotation.walkthrough: TT is short for teetotaller, not the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
annotation.definitionFit: A strict teetotaller is always stone-cold sober.

entries.clue: TV etc showing recurring image: ex-royal Alexandra's butt (3,5)

indicatorNotes.butt: the butt is the end, so the last letter of Alexandra

blocks.note: Princess Diana, formerly of the royal family

annotation.surface: Television keeps running a picture of a former royal's bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ex-royal Alexandra' reads as one person; the ex-royal is Di and Alexandra only gives up her last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: TV is one branch of the mass media, and 'etc' widens it to press and radio.

entries.clue: (& 1dn.) Balls possibly in line of fire from such an unthinking response? (4,4)

blocks.clueFragment: Balls possibly in line of fire
blocks.note: read literally: a groin is exactly where an upward-jerking knee lands
read as meant: a reflex reaction, the one a doctor tests by tapping below the kneecap

annotation.surface: A warning that someone's testicles are in the path of a reflex.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke takes 'knee-jerk' literally: a knee flying up makes the groin the target. The phrase itself means an automatic, unconsidered reaction.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the automatic kick of the patellar reflex became the standard phrase for any response made without thought.

entries.clue: Strip clubs inside bar entrance (5)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'clubs inside' means the clubs letter is placed within the strip

blocks.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

annotation.surface: Directions to the strip clubs found just inside a pub's door.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strip clubs' is a single phrase in the surface; split it, and 'bar entrance' becomes a verb phrase, not a pub door.
annotation.definitionFit: To latch a door is to fasten it, barring the entrance.

entries.clue: Flash's uniform accommodating large body (6)

indicatorNotes.accommodating: to accommodate is to give room to, as a hotel houses guests, so the large body sits within the uniform

blocks.note: flat = uniform, as in a flat rate
the UN, a large international body

annotation.surface: Flash, the comic-book hero or the cad, has a costume roomy enough for a big physique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' suggests a costume or the letter U; here it is FLAT, and 'large body' is the United Nations.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to flash your wealth is to display it showily, just as you would parade it.

entries.clue: For sale: kinky casual wear (7)

indicatorNotes.kinky: twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

annotation.surface: A small ad offering fetish gear that is comfortable enough to wear every day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' sets up a naughty listing; loafers are slip-on shoes.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: laceless slip-on shoes are a staple of relaxed, off-duty dress.

entries.clue: Guardsman finally eases off penetration (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: picks the final letter of Guardsman
indicatorNotes.off: 'eases off' means gently removes, so that letter comes away from the soldier

blocks.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard
last letter of Guardsman, removed from SENTRY

annotation.surface: A soldier at last relaxes his grip on an invasion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guardsman' does two jobs: as a whole it is SENTRY, and its final letter is the S that goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: penetration is the act of getting in, and the surface's sexual sense fits the puzzle's bawdy tone.

entries.clue: Speaker's stand on unstable sort being introduced to drink (7)

indicatorNotes.unstable: the letters of SORT wobble into a new order
indicatorNotes.being introduced to: introducing one thing to another brings it in, so the shuffled sort goes into the drink

annotation.surface: The Speaker's view on a wobbly type who has been handed a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's stand' reads as the Speaker's opinion; it is the platform a speaker stands on.
annotation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker.

entries.clue: Rooftop game: letting bastard go (5)

indicatorNotes.letting: 'letting … go' means releasing, so the bastard's letter is let out of the game

blocks.note: b = bastard, as in the abbreviated expletive

annotation.surface: A rooftop game being played until some rotter is allowed to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: B for bastard is the abbreviation used in printed swearing ('you b——').
annotation.definitionFit: The ridge is the top edge of a roof.

entries.clue: see 2dn. (5)
Turned out lousy, being in need of instruction (9)

indicatorNotes.lousy: poor, bad, so the letters are in a poor order

annotation.surface: Someone did badly because they had never been taught properly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like the anagram indicator; it is the fodder, and 'lousy' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: someone never taught lacks schooling and so still needs lessons.

entries.clue: Screwed on entering appropriate place? (5)

indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go into, so 'on' goes into the bed

blocks.note: bed is the appropriate place for screwing

annotation.surface: A question of whether some act of penetration took place in the right spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate place' is a cheeky cryptic hint for BED, fitting the definition's sense.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Boned' is slang for having had sex, i.e. screwed.

entries.clue: Only recently painted as tasteless? (5)

blocks.note: fresh paint has not dried and is still slightly sticky

annotation.surface: A sniffy remark that a newly decorated room is in poor taste.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the two meanings as though one explained the other: the room is tacky in both senses.
annotation.definitionFit: Tacky means tasteless and cheap-looking.

entries.clue: Entrepreneur (as Ian?) protects massive land area (7)

indicatorNotes.protects: the phrase holds the answer within it, guarding it

annotation.surface: A businessman, perhaps one called Ian, looks after a huge territory.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside looks like a name guess; it is there to supply the hidden letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Eurasia, Europe and Asia together, is the largest land mass.
